newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway stocks buck trend, break new record ground.
newsitem.headline: Norway stocks buck trend, break new record ground.

text.p: Norwegian shares reversed an early slide and moved into new record territory on Thursday, despite a negative trend on most major stock exchanges and a dip in the dollar, as investors continued to plough money into the market.
Oslo's Total share index rose 0.41 percent to 1,128.46 points, a new peak. Turnover was a hefty 1.45 billion crowns.

Star performers were in the offshore sector with Smedvig topping the list. Smedvig announced it had signed a letter of intent with Shell Deepwater Development Inc. of the United States for a long-term deep water drilling contract in the Gulf of Mexico.
The assignment will run for five years and has an estimated value of 2.1 billion crowns. Smedvig said the deal was a breakthrough first drilling assignment for the company in the U.S. market.
The company's share price advanced five crowns to 172 crowns in 90.2 million crowns of trade. The B share closed up 4.29 percent at 170 crowns in turnover of 117 million crowns.
Industrial heavyweight Norsk Hydro also was on the winners' list, climbing eight crowns to 381 crowns in business worth 101 million crowns.
